focus_areas: Negative verification of dorsal fin and pectoral fins

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Focus heavily on the texture of the skin. Real grey whales have very specific, irregular white patches caused by parasites. AI often generates generic 'noise' or uniform speckling. Verify if the white patches look like distinct biological entities (barnacles) or just digital noise. Also, scrutinize the water splash—AI struggles with coherent water droplets; look for smeared or fused water elements. CRITICAL: Use the open vocabulary detector to explicitly confirm there is NO dorsal fin and NO pectoral fins visible; their absence is a key identifier for Grey Whales in this cropped view.
image_description: A vertical close-up shot of a grey whale breaching or spy-hopping in deep blue ocean water. The whale's head and upper torso are visible above the surface, oriented vertically with the rostrum pointing upward. The skin is dark grey/black with significant white mottling (barnacles/lice). Water splashes around the base where the body meets the surface.
